We need a compiled electron-cyclotron (EC) reference before generating heating
and current profiles for transport. The [Primer](../primer.qmd) explains that
coupling; terminology is in the [Glossary](../glossary.qmd).

We built a local executable for the external reference:
[one external reference executable builds with verified artifacts and resolved runtime libraries]{.claim}[C-154](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-154){.cid .st-measured}. The build uses a pinned replacement plotting library,
Giza, with the available compiler and NetCDF libraries. Source files stay
unchanged; recorded compiler flags permit the legacy Fortran interfaces.
The compiler's warnings remain in the retained logs.

Build preparation uses one CPU, an isolated working directory and a five-minute
deadline. The final build finishes in about 66 seconds. Its executed helper,
source archives, binary, plotting libraries and logs have content-bound provenance.
Two earlier builds are retained: their source-snapshot lineage was corrected
in the final build rather than rewriting old records.

A concrete request now proposes one unchanged upstream ITER regression case.
The original current-drive prescription is proposed because a paired saved
output exists for inspection. This remains the owner's physics choice. The
requested job uses one CPU, four GiB and ten minutes, with a five-minute solver
timeout. Charging may cover a whole node, so the approval request states that
resource ceiling too.

The submission launcher checks hashes of the binary, input decks, libraries,
toolkit source and job scripts before execution. Its read-only preparation check
passes. These build and linkage checks inspect the produced files separately
from compilation; they do not exercise the solver's plotting or physics paths.
A job would retain native outputs, failures, logs and CPU/job metadata in a new
directory. At this checkpoint, no job has been submitted and GENRAY has not been run.

A compiled executable establishes build readiness. Plotting parity, solver
outputs, physical acceptance and transport-source conversion still need review.
The independent ITER pedestal port still awaits its boundary choices.
Historical test statistics are unchanged, and M3 remains in progress.
The subsequent [first-run failure](33-genray-first-run-plotting-failure.qmd)
and [corrected result](34-genray-corrected-numerical-pilot.qmd) are recorded separately.

Technical details → [reference build and pilot request](../technical/surrogates.qmd#genray-build).
